title: jingyaogong/minimind
lede: MiniMind is a PyTorch-native project for training a 64M-parameter language model from scratch on one consumer GPU, with every training stage written out in plain code as a hands-on LLM course.

points: The headline two hours is one SFT epoch on a single RTX 3090, at about 3 yuan of rented GPU time, per the README.
Code covers pretraining, SFT, LoRA, DPO, PPO, GRPO and CISPO, tool use, agentic RL and distillation, without high-level library wrappers.
minimind-3 follows the Qwen3 architecture, in a 64M dense model and a 198M mixture-of-experts model with 64M active.
Weights load in transformers, llama.cpp, vLLM and Ollama, and the repo includes an OpenAI-compatible server and a Streamlit chat UI.
Training datasets are published, with mini versions sized for a quick reproduction.

points.text: Many open threads are not bugs but shared training logs, experiment results and tutorials from people reproducing the model.
Users ask how to teach the small model narrow skills, such as addition and subtraction under 100.
Others want guidance on adjusting the model's parameter configuration for their own runs.
